title: Problem Overview: Khintchine's Equidistribution Conjecture
content: Erdős Problem #994 asks whether Khintchine's 1923 conjecture is true: for almost all $\alpha$, does the sequence $\{k\alpha\}$ equidistribute in every measurable $E \subseteq (0,1)$? Marstrand (1970) showed this is FALSE—the quantifiers $\forall E$ and $\forall^{\text{a.e.}} \alpha$ cannot be exchanged.
mathContext: The conjecture asks whether $\forall^{\text{a.e.}} \alpha,\; \forall E \text{ meas.},\; \frac{1}{n}|\{k \leq n : \{k\alpha\} \in E\}| \to \lambda(E)$. This is the quantifier reversal of Weyl's theorem.

title: Fractional Part Function
content: Defines $\{x\} = x - \lfloor x \rfloor$, the fractional part of a real number. This is the fundamental operation underlying equidistribution modulo 1. The formalization uses Lean's `Int.floor` for the floor function.

title: Fractional Part Bounds
content: Two proved theorems establishing that $0 \leq \{x\} < 1$ for all $x$. `frac_nonneg` uses `Int.floor_le` ($\lfloor x \rfloor \leq x$) and `frac_lt_one` uses `Int.sub_one_lt_floor` ($x - 1 < \lfloor x \rfloor$). These are among the few fully proved results in the file.

title: Fractional Part Sequence
content: Defines $\{k\alpha\}_{k=1}^{\infty}$, the sequence of fractional parts of multiples of $\alpha$. This is the object studied by Weyl's equidistribution theorem (1916). For irrational $\alpha$, this sequence is dense in $[0,1)$ and equidistributed in intervals.
mathContext: $\text{fracSequence}(\alpha, k) = \{k\alpha\} = k\alpha - \lfloor k\alpha \rfloor$. For irrational $\alpha$, the orbit $\{\{k\alpha\}\}_{k \geq 1}$ is dense in $[0,1)$.

title: Indicator Function
content: Defines $\mathbf{1}_E(x) = 1$ if $x \in E$, $0$ otherwise. Used to count hits: $\sum_{k=1}^n \mathbf{1}_E(\{k\alpha\})$ is the number of fractional parts landing in $E$.

title: Count of Hits in E
content: Counts how many of $\{\alpha\}, \{2\alpha\}, \ldots, \{n\alpha\}$ fall in $E$, implemented using `Finset.range n` filtered by the membership predicate. The shift `k + 1` ensures we count from $k = 1$ (since `Finset.range n` gives $0, 1, \ldots, n-1$).

title: Empirical Frequency
content: Normalizes the count by $n$ to get the empirical frequency $\frac{1}{n}|\{k \leq n : \{k\alpha\} \in E\}|$. Equidistribution means this converges to $\lambda(E)$ as $n \to \infty$.

title: Equidistribution Predicate
content: Defines `IsEquidistributed α E μ` as `Tendsto (empiricalFrequency α E) atTop (nhds μ)`: the empirical frequency converges to $\mu = \lambda(E)$ in the topology of $\mathbb{R}$. This is the precise limit condition that both Weyl and Khintchine concern.

title: Weyl's Equidistribution Theorem (Axiomatized)
content: Axiomatizes Weyl's theorem: for any fixed measurable $E \subseteq (0,1)$, the sequence $\{k\alpha\}$ is equidistributed in $E$ for almost every $\alpha$. The exceptional null set $N_E$ depends on $E$—this is precisely what Khintchine tried to strengthen.

title: Weyl's Statement as Proposition
content: Packages Weyl's theorem as a single proposition `WeylStatement`: for all measurable $E \subseteq (0,1)$, almost every $\alpha$ gives equidistribution. The quantifier order is $\forall E,\; \forall^{\text{a.e.}} \alpha$.

title: Weyl's Theorem is True
content: Proves `weyl_is_true : WeylStatement` by introducing $E$ and its measurability/containment hypotheses, then applying the `weyl_theorem` axiom. This is a simple wrapper making the axiom usable as a named theorem.

title: Khintchine's Conjecture
content: Defines `KhintchineConjecture` as $\forall^{\text{a.e.}} \alpha,\; \forall E$ (measurable, $\subseteq (0,1)$), equidistribution holds. This reverses the quantifier order from Weyl's theorem. The conjecture asks: can the exceptional null set be chosen independently of $E$?

title: Khintchine's Conjecture (Explicit Null Set)
content: An equivalent formulation making the null set explicit: $\exists S$ with $\lambda(S) = 0$ such that for all $\alpha \notin S$ and all measurable $E \subseteq (0,1)$, equidistribution holds. This makes clear that the conjecture asks for a single universal null set $S$.

title: Weyl Quantifier Order
content: Makes the quantifier order of Weyl's theorem explicit: $\forall E,\; \forall^{\text{a.e.}} \alpha$ (for each set, almost all $\alpha$ work). The null set $N_E = \{\alpha : \alpha \text{ fails for } E\}$ depends on $E$.
mathContext: $\text{WeylOrder} \equiv \forall E,\; \forall^{\text{a.e.}} \alpha,\; \text{IsEquidistributed}(\alpha, E, \lambda(E))$. The null set $N_E$ satisfies $\lambda(N_E) = 0$ but may vary with $E$.

title: Khintchine Quantifier Order
content: Makes Khintchine's quantifier order explicit: $\forall^{\text{a.e.}} \alpha,\; \forall E$ (almost all $\alpha$ work for every set simultaneously). This would require a single null set $N$ independent of $E$—which Marstrand showed is impossible.
mathContext: $\text{KhintchineOrder} \equiv \forall^{\text{a.e.}} \alpha,\; \forall E \text{ meas.},\; \text{IsEquidistributed}(\alpha, E, \lambda(E))$. Would need $N = \bigcap_E N_E^c$ to have full measure.

title: Quantifier Exchange Fails
content: Axiomatizes the key negative result: even though `WeylOrder` is true, `KhintchineOrder` does not follow. This captures the mathematical essence of the problem: $\forall E\; \forall^{\text{a.e.}} \alpha \not\Rightarrow \forall^{\text{a.e.}} \alpha\; \forall E$.
mathContext: $\text{WeylOrder} \Rightarrow \neg\text{KhintchineOrder}$. The implication $\text{WeylOrder} \Rightarrow \text{KhintchineOrder}$ fails because $\bigcup_E N_E$ can have positive measure.

title: Marstrand's Disproof
content: Axiomatizes Marstrand's 1970 result: `¬KhintchineConjecture`. The Khintchine conjecture is FALSE. Marstrand showed that for any irrational $\alpha$, one can construct a measurable $E_\alpha$ (depending on the continued fraction expansion of $\alpha$) where equidistribution fails.
mathContext: $\neg\text{KhintchineConjecture}$: there is no null set $S$ such that $\forall \alpha \notin S,\; \forall E,\; f_n(\alpha, E) \to \lambda(E)$

title: Marstrand's Construction (Existential Witness)
content: Axiomatizes the existence of a specific counterexample: there exist $\alpha$ and measurable $E \subseteq (0,1)$ such that $\{k\alpha\}$ is NOT equidistributed in $E$. This is the constructive content of Marstrand's proof.
mathContext: $\exists \alpha,\; \exists E \text{ meas.} \subseteq (0,1),\; \lim_{n \to \infty} f_n(\alpha, E) \neq \lambda(E)$ (or the limit does not exist)

title: Bad Set Exists for Every Irrational α
content: The strongest form of the disproof: for EVERY irrational $\alpha$, there exists a measurable 'bad' set $E_\alpha$ where equidistribution fails. This shows the failure is universal, not restricted to special $\alpha$. The construction of $E_\alpha$ uses the specific continued fraction expansion of $\alpha$.

title: Failure Mechanism: Exceptional Sets and Avoidance
content: Two placeholder definitions documenting the mechanism behind the failure. `exceptionalSetIssue` notes that while each $N_E$ has measure zero, $\bigcup_E N_E$ over uncountably many measurable $E$ can have positive measure. `avoidanceConstruction` notes that Marstrand builds $E$ by 'tracking' the continued fraction convergents of $\alpha$.
mathContext: The uncountable union issue: $\lambda(N_E) = 0$ for each $E$, but $\lambda(\bigcup_E N_E)$ may be positive. Countable additivity does not apply to uncountable unions.

title: Weyl Equidistribution for Intervals
content: Axiomatizes Weyl's original result for intervals: for any irrational $\alpha$ and any subinterval $(a,b) \subseteq [0,1]$, the empirical frequency converges to $b - a$. Note: this holds for ALL irrational $\alpha$, with no exceptional set—a stark contrast to the measurable set case.
mathContext: $\forall \alpha \text{ irrational},\; \forall 0 \leq a < b \leq 1,\; \lim_{n \to \infty} f_n(\alpha, (a,b)) = b - a$. No exceptional set needed.
